descriptionChirho: A proper noun referring to Zelophehad (tselofchad), a man of the tribe of Manasseh who died in the wilderness leaving only daughters, whose case established the legal precedent for female inheritance in Israel (Num 26:33; 27:1,7; 36:2,6,10,11; Josh 17:3; 1 Chr 7:15). All three clusters are syntactic variants: bare nominative 'Zelophehad/Tselofejad' (S130170), prepositional/bare 'to Tselofchad/Tselofchad' (S130171), and conjunctive 'and for/and Zelophehad' (S130172). Multilingual evidence uniformly identifies one person: 'सलोफहाद/सलापहाद' (hin), 'صَلَفْحَادَ' (arb), '스록버하드/신로비하드' (kor), 'Selofehadi' (swa), 'Tselofejad/Zelofejad' (spa).
